title: 30 Money Rules to Live By in 2027
description:
Forget vague New Year's resolutions. Here are 30 simple money rules to live by in 2027, in three groups: 10 rules about the numbers (emergency fund, the 15% rule, the rule of 72, the 20/4/10 car rule, your FI number), 10 rules about psychology (pay yourself first, the 48-hour rule, why scams cost Americans over $12 billion in 2024), and 10 action rules to protect and grow your money.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:07 Why rules beat resolutions
2:01 How we got the numbers
2:25 Angle 1: The Numbers
2:28 Rule 1. Keep 3 to 6 months of essentials in cash
3:25 Rule 2. Save at least 15% for retirement
4:18 Rule 3. Never leave the match on the table
5:04 Rule 4. Pay off any debt above about 8%
5:53 Rule 5. Keep housing around 30% of gross income or less
6:52 Rule 6. Use the rule of 72
7:43 Rule 7. Keep investment fees as low as possible
8:53 Rule 8. Keep total car costs under control
9:51 Rule 9. Know your number: 25 times spending
10:42 Rule 10. Check your net worth once a year
11:30 Angle 2: The Psychology
11:34 Rule 11. Pay yourself first
12:17 Rule 12. Spend extravagantly on what you love, cut mercilessly on what you don't
13:06 Rule 13. Wait 48 hours before big purchases
13:53 Rule 14. Don't compare your finances to social media
14:37 Rule 15. If it sounds too good to be true, it is
15:45 Rule 16. Time in the market beats timing the market
16:30 Rule 17. Never invest in what you can't explain
17:11 Rule 18. Automate every good decision
17:58 Rule 19. Let your lifestyle rise slower than your income
18:40 Rule 20. Money is a tool, not a scoreboard
19:28 A quick favor
19:39 Angle 3: The Playbook
19:45 Rule 21. Check your credit reports regularly
20:25 Rule 22. Freeze your credit
21:10 Rule 23. Insure against catastrophe, not inconvenience
22:02 Rule 24. Name your beneficiaries and have a will
22:50 Rule 25. Always negotiate
23:39 Rule 26. Use tax advantaged accounts first
24:31 Rule 27. Review subscriptions twice a year
25:12 Rule 28. Build sinking funds for predictable costs
25:55 Rule 29. Talk about money with the people you share life with
26:39 Rule 30. Invest in yourself every year
27:48 A month by month plan for 2027
28:55 What a year of rules can do
30:10 Questions people ask
31:34 Recap: all 30 rules
33:47 What to do next

Sources:
- Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households (SHED), $400 emergency question
- Federal Reserve, G.19 Consumer Credit (credit card interest rates)
- Federal Trade Commission, Consumer Sentinel Network data on fraud losses (2024)
- U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Expenditure Survey (housing share)
- William P. Bengen, Determining Withdrawal Rates Using Historical Data (1994)
- Fidelity, retirement savings guidelines by age
- Ramit Sethi, I Will Teach You to Be Rich (conscious spending)
- Richard H. Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi, Save More Tomorrow (2004)
- Elizabeth Dunn and Michael Norton, Happy Money (2013)
- AnnualCreditReport.com and FTC guidance on free credit freezes
- C+R Research, subscription spending survey (2022)
- IRS, annual contribution limits for 401(k), IRA and HSA
